title: Add a `range` function to generate integer arrays
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->

### Use Cases

Some inputs encode integer sets as compact ranges, for example `"500..512"` or `"1-4094"`. Expanding them into the list of integers is not possible in VRL today.

### Attempted Solutions

VRL has no way to create an array of N integers (`range(1, 4)` returns error E105, undefined function), and `for_each` only iterates over a collection that already exists. The only workaround we found is to embed a literal array of all possible values and `slice` it.

### Proposal

Add a `range` function to the stdlib, similar to Python's `range`:

```coffee
range(start: integer, end: integer, [step: integer = 1]) :: array, fallible
```

- Half-open: `range(500, 513)` returns `[500, 501, ..., 512]`.
- `step` can be negative: `range(5, 0, -1)` returns `[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]`.
- It errors if `step == 0`, and if the result would exceed a size limit, to protect against memory exhaustion. The limit is open for discussion: a fixed maximum, or an optional argument.
- An empty range returns `[]`.

Example:

```coffee
bounds = split(string!(.ids), "..")
.ids = range!(to_int!(bounds[0]), to_int!(bounds[1]) + 1)
```

We would be happy to submit a PR for this.

### References

- #1297 (`break` in iterations): related, since iteration in VRL is limited to existing collections.

title: Lexer panics on non-ASCII char in column-0 comment inside a block ("is not a char boundary", lex.rs:923)
body:
## Description

Since VRL 0.36.0 (shipped in Vector 0.59.0), the lexer panics on a valid program that contains a non-ASCII character in a comment. The same program compiles and runs fine on VRL 0.35.0 / Vector 0.58.0.

```
thread 'main' panicked at vrl-0.36.0/src/parser/lex.rs:923:47:
start byte index 35 is not a char boundary; it is inside '—' (bytes 34..37 of string)
```

In Vector this makes `vector validate` / `vector test` panic, and a config containing such a `remap` transform crashes the whole topology at startup.

## Reproduction

`repro.vrl`:

```coffee
x = {}
if !is_object(x) {
# a
# b — c
  .a = 1
}
.a
```

```sh
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w timberio/vector:0.58.0-alpine vrl --input /dev/null --program /w/repro.vrl
# null

docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w timberio/vector:0.59.0-alpine vrl --input /dev/null --program /w/repro.vrl
# thread 'main' panicked at .../vrl-0.36.0/src/parser/lex.rs:923:47:
# start byte index 35 is not a char boundary; it is inside '—' (bytes 34..37 of string)
```

Observations:
- At least two consecutive comment lines are needed, and they must start at column 0. Indenting them makes the panic go away.
- The non-ASCII character must be in the second comment.
- With an ASCII-only second comment, there is no panic.

## Analysis

`delimited_query_char` (introduced in 2cc1119, "chore(lints): remove parser pedantic exceptions (#1946)") slices the input before checking which character is at `pos`:

```rust
let mut lexer = Lexer::new(&self.input[pos + 1..]);   // lex.rs:923
let (result, description) = if input.starts_with('"') {
    ...
} else {
    return Ok(chars.peek().expect("query character is present").1);
};
```

`pos + 1` is only a valid char boundary when the character at `pos` is ASCII. Before #1946, the `Lexer::new(&self.input[pos + 1..])` calls were inside the `'"'`/`s'`/`r'`/`t'` branches, so they only ever ran after a single-byte character.

A non-ASCII character reaches this code because of how comments are skipped in the delimited-query scan. The `#` branch consumes the first comment up to and including `\n`. The caller then calls `chars.next()`, which eats the `#` of the next comment as an ordinary character. The rest of that comment line is then scanned char by char, and the first multi-byte character panics.

So there are probably two issues:
1. **Panic:** the slice should move into the branches that need it, or `pos + ch.len_utf8()` should be used.
2. **Comment handling:** a comment directly after another comment at column 0 isn't recognised as a comment during this lookahead. This is harmless for ASCII, but it is still incorrect.

The code is unchanged on current `main`.

## Versions

- Vector 0.59.0 (`timberio/vector:0.59.0-alpine`), VRL 0.36.0: panics
- Vector 0.58.0 (`timberio/vector:0.58.0-alpine`): OK

title: `uuid_v7(timestamp)` encodes incorrect Unix milliseconds
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

`uuid_v7(timestamp)` does not correctly encode the input timestamp in the UUIDv7 timestamp field.

UUIDv7 stores Unix milliseconds in its first 48 bits. For `2026-01-01T00:00:00.123456789Z`, the UUID should start with `019b76da-a87b-7`, but the generated UUID has a different timestamp prefix.

The input timestamp should be preserved with millisecond precision.

### VRL Program

```text
id = uuid_v7(t'2026-01-01T00:00:00.123456789Z')
prefix = replace(slice!(string!(id), 0, 13), "-", "")
assert_eq!(prefix, "019b76daa87b")
```

VRL 0.35.0 (current upstream main)

title: Release tool: validate crates.io token authenticity (or restructure flow so we don't need to)
body:
## Context

Pre-flight in #1858 was originally supposed to validate that the configured crates.io token is valid before mutating anything. Two attempts didn't work:

1. `cargo owner --list vrl` — unauthenticated on crates.io (`GET /api/v1/crates/{name}/owners` runs `list_owners` with no auth check).
2. `GET /api/v1/me` — uses `AuthCheck::only_cookie()` and rejects API-token auth outright.

A search of the crates.io controllers (`rust-lang/crates.io`) found no non-mutating endpoint that accepts an API token: every `AuthCheck::default()` route is either a mutation (`POST /api/v1/crates/new` publish, `PUT/DELETE /api/v1/crates/{name}/owners`, `POST /api/v1/me/tokens` create) or a destructive delete (`DELETE /api/v1/tokens/current` revokes the token you just used to authenticate).

So today's pre-flight is a presence check only — it catches "never ran `cargo login`" (the failure mode from the 0.34.0 release) but not "token expired" or "token has wrong scope". Those still surface at `cargo publish` after the version bump and changelog commits are made.

## Options

### A. Ugly-but-benign probe

`POST /api/v1/me/tokens` runs `AuthCheck::default()` first, then rejects API-token callers with 400 ("cannot use an API token to create a new API token"). No side effects. This means:
- Valid token → 400 with that specific body
- Invalid token → 401
- Would need to send a placeholder request body

Downsides: relies on internal ordering of checks; fragile if crates.io reorganizes.

### B. Restructure flow so a failed publish leaves no state

If `cargo publish` runs before the release commits, or if the commits auto-rollback on publish failure, the whole "did they run `cargo login`" check becomes moot. Sketch:

1. Bump `Cargo.toml` (in-tree, uncommitted).
2. `cargo publish --allow-dirty` — this is what actually validates auth.
3. If publish succeeded: commit version, generate changelog, commit, tag, push, PR.
4. If publish failed: `git checkout -- Cargo.toml Cargo.lock` and exit.

Also solves the checkpointing problem from #1859 for this specific failure.

### C. Live with the presence check

Document the limitation and accept that expired/wrong-scope tokens fail at `cargo publish`. Combined with #1859 (resume-from-checkpoint), the manual recovery cost is much lower.

## Recommendation

B is the cleanest — it removes an entire class of failure rather than trying to detect it. C is the do-nothing fallback if B turns out to be more disruptive than expected.

### Problem


Using vector (0.54), a transform wasn't compiling and I wasn't really understanding the error message. I managed to distill it down to this minimal example : (you can use any fallible function, I used to_float as an example)

When compiled and run : adding it to the `fixme` folder and running `cargo run --package vrl-tests --bin vrl-tests -- --pattern 'fixme'`

we get this compile error

```
warning[E900]: unused variable `err`
  ┌─ :1:4
  │
1 │ p, err = to_float(.message)
  │    ^^^ help: use the result of this expression or remove it
  │
  = this expression has no side-effects
  = see language documentation at https://vrl.dev
  = try your code in the VRL REPL, learn more at https://vrl.dev/examples
```
The `err` variable is used though 🤔  (we assign .e to its value)

The compile error goes away when removing the err = "" line, which suggests to me that it might be an unexpected scoping rule, and the reassignement of the err variable interferes with the "unused code analysis"

The error also does not appear on the VRL playground, only when running `vector` ( or a vrl unit test)


### VRL Program

```text

.p = p
.e = err

title: `http_request` retry policy discards first OK request
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

Behavior observed with the following scripts

server
```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Simple HTTP server that returns 500 N times before returning 200.

Usage: python3 flaky_server.py <fail_count> [port]
  fail_count  number of 500 responses before returning 200
  port        port to listen on (default: 8080)
"""

import sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

fail_count = 0
request_count = 0


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        global request_count
        request_count += 1
        if request_count % (fail_count + 1) != 0:
            self.send_response(500)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(f"Error (attempt {request_count}/{fail_count})\n".encode())
            print(f"Request {request_count}: 500")
        else:
            self.send_response(200)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b"OK\n")
            print(f"Request {request_count}: 200")

    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        pass  # suppress default access log


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print(__doc__)
        sys.exit(1)

    fail_count = int(sys.argv[1])
    port = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 8080

    print(f"Listening on :{port} — will 500 for first {fail_count} request(s)")
    HTTPServer(("", port), Handler).serve_forever()
```

## Reproducer:

Start the server
```sh
./scripts/flaky_server.py 2
```

Run vrl
```sh
echo 'http_request!("http://localhost:8080/")' | cargo run -p vrl-cli -q -- -q
```

output:
```
Listening on :8080 — will 500 for first 2 request(s)
Request 1: 500
Request 2: 500
Request 3: 200
Request 4: 500
Request 5: 500
Request 6: 200

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

We often perform selective flattening for our payloads, meaning that we often need to exclude certain keys during the flattening operation. Currently this requires a somewhat verbose save/restore dance:

```coffee
metadata = del(.metadata)
tags = del(.tags)

. = compact(flatten(., "_"))

.metadata = metadata
.tags = tags
```

This is also useful for downstream consumers that do not necessarily want to flatten specific fields and instead want to store them within a JSON record/column.

### Attempted Solutions

_No response_

### Proposal

Add an optional `except` parameter to flatten that accepts an array of key names to exclude from flattening:

```coffee
. = compact(flatten(., "_", except: ["metadata", "tags"]))
```

Keys matching the except list would be preserved as-is while everything else is flattened normally.

_No response_

title: `Example` should take in an optional input
body:
In #1564, a bunch of examples were synced from the Vector repo. However, some examples where using an input before and the workaround for this was to add a `. = { "foo": "bar" }` to simulate the input. This is a bit misleading because it gives type information that VRL would usually not have when parsing events coming in from the input.

See the [Valid Boolean from path](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/pull/1564/changes#diff-d9839640b8c46c4dbd7d5b39b0eb36ddb2fc06eb3b6a9fbf22370d27d3b8b1e1) example and the [equivalent example in the Vector repo](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/d10f3a5b892833232002c97f24bf008dbef1eeec/website/cue/reference/remap/functions/bool.cue#L28-L37) for a reference.

<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

When given somewhat nonsensical values, `parse_duration` can cause panics in vector and crash the process.  Attempting to parse those values should fail, but not cause the process to die.  Below is a simple repro using vector 0.52.0:

```

thread 'main' (803763) panicked at /cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/rust_decimal-1.39.0/src/arithmetic_impls.rs:232:18:

  17:     0x558ef1af9d12 - vrl::cli::cmd::run::h82eba3f13ec0c79c

In our case, we were using `parse_duration` (probably overzealously) in a section of code that generically tries to transform arbitrary strings into "better" values by just attempting a few things:

```
typed = map_values(object(parsed), recursive: true) -> |value| {
  parse_int(value) ?? parse_float(value) ?? parse_duration(value, "s") ?? value
}
```

After years of stability, seemingly out of nowhere, our entire fleet went down, presumably after receiving a bunch of logs which had fields that would crash `parse_duration` as the value above does.  It wasn't trivial to determine the source but once we did it was fairly easy to reproduce.

title: Escaping characters in parse_cef?
body:
Hi.

I am trying to get the parse_cef() function to escape characters, but I am unable to get it to parse fields that include `=` such as: `... cs4=None request="https://foo.com?id=foo&a=bar" abc=lol`

Here is a link to the VRL Playground with example data: [link](https://playground.vrl.dev/?%%)

If I am not mistaken CEF-formatted data should include quotes for data that requires it (as it does in my example) but I cannot get Vector to parse it correctly and have run out of ideas to test.

Currently all CEF-formatted URL logs that include parameters are being dropped by the transformer and is what I am trying to fix.

There is a chance I have overlooked something here, but from what I could see the only option to adjust the parse_cef function is `translate_custom_fields` which unfortunately does not help much in this case.

Is it possible to use parse_cef or is it better to go with a custom transformer such as the one mentioned in [#6451](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/issues/6451#issue-809083142)?

title: FR: Allow http_request function to send request body

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

The http_request function in VRL currently allows making HTTP requests by specifying method, headers, and URL. However, it does not support sending a request body.

This limits its use mainly to GET or HEAD operations and makes it impossible to interact with endpoints that require a payload in POST, PUT, or PATCH requests.

Benefits:

Enables full interaction with REST APIs directly from VRL.
Reduces the need for external processors to enrich or validate data.
Increases VRL’s flexibility in enrichment and transformation scenarios.

Expected impact:
Backward compatible: existing usage remains unchanged if body is not provided.
Adds significant value without breaking existing functionality.

### Use Cases

My current use case is to send the logs to an external anonymizer 

### Attempted Solutions

I had to change the current service to accept values via query string

### Proposal

Proposal:
Introduce an optional body parameter to the http_request function that would accept:

A plain string (e.g., serialized JSON).

(Optionally) a map that can be automatically serialized depending on the Content-Type.

### References

https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/pull/1360

title: The AWS ALB log format has changed again!
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

Vector started getting upset about this a few hours ago:

```
"function call error for \"parse_aws_alb_log\" at (4:32): Log should be fully consumed: \" \"-\" \"-\" \"-\"\""
```

Sure enough, the format has changed! Not universally, but somewhere around 1% of our logs have new elements after the TID:

```
https 2025-08-19T21:34:47.383127Z some/alb/target 1.23.45.67:12345 10.20.30.40:8080 0.010 0.005 0.000 200 200 496 340 "GET https://example.com:443/url/path HTTP/1.1" "User/Agent" SSL-CIPHERS TLSv1.2 arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-feast-1:123456789012:targetgroup/target-group-name/some-id "Root=1-12345678-123456789012345678901234" "example.com" "arn:aws:acm:us-best-2:123456789012:certificate/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012" 20 2025-08-19T21:34:47.367000Z "some_action,forward" "-" "-" "10.20.30.40:8080" "200" "-" "-" TID_12345678901234567890123456789012 "-" "-" "-"
```

^ The above has been heavily anonymized, but the punchline is the part after the TID. Compare this to a log from AWS' [own documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html#access-log-entry-examples) that I'm looking at _right this moment_ that does not yet describe the new elements:

```
http 2018-07-02T22:23:00.186641Z app/my-loadbalancer/50dc6c495c0c9188 
192.168.131.39:2817 10.0.0.1:80 0.000 0.001 0.000 200 200 34 366 
"GET http://www.example.com:80/ HTTP/1.1" "curl/7.46.0" - - 
arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-2:123456789012:targetgroup/my-targets/73e2d6bc24d8a067
"Root=1-58337262-36d228ad5d99923122bbe354" "-" "-" 
0 2018-07-02T22:22:48.364000Z "forward" "-" "-" "10.0.0.1:80" "200" "-" "-" TID_1234abcd5678ef90
```

In the AWS example, `TID_1234abcd5678ef90` is the last element. What are the new mystery elements? Who knows! I suppose they might contain values other than `-` in the future, but for now I haven't seen any information about them.

Sample VRL program below demonstrates a parseable log where the last element is the TID is the last element, and can be parsed, and another log that is unparseable because of the new elements.

Vector version taken from whatever was running on VRL playground today.

### VRL Program

```text
parseable = "https 2025-08-19T21:34:47.383127Z some/alb/target 1.23.45.67:12345 10.20.30.40:8080 0.010 0.005 0.000 200 200 496 340 \"GET https://example.com:443/url/path HTTP/1.1\" \"User/Agent\" SSL-CIPHERS TLSv1.2 arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-feast-1:123456789012:targetgroup/target-group-name/some-id \"Root=1-12345678-123456789012345678901234\" \"example.com\" \"arn:aws:acm:us-best-2:123456789012:certificate/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012\" 20 2025-08-19T21:34:47.367000Z \"some_action,forward\" \"-\" \"-\" \"10.20.30.40:8080\" \"200\" \"-\" \"-\" TID_12345678901234567890123456789012"
unparseable = "https 2025-08-19T21:34:47.383127Z some/alb/target 1.23.45.67:12345 10.20.30.40:8080 0.010 0.005 0.000 200 200 496 340 \"GET https://example.com:443/url/path HTTP/1.1\" \"User/Agent\" SSL-CIPHERS TLSv1.2 arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-feast-1:123456789012:targetgroup/target-group-name/some-id \"Root=1-12345678-123456789012345678901234\" \"example.com\" \"arn:aws:acm:us-best-2:123456789012:certificate/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012\" 20 2025-08-19T21:34:47.367000Z \"some_action,forward\" \"-\" \"-\" \"10.20.30.40:8080\" \"200\" \"-\" \"-\" TID_12345678901234567890123456789012 \"-\" \"-\" \"-\""

# This succeeds!
.good = parse_aws_alb_log!(parseable)

# This does not!
.bad, err = parse_aws_alb_log(unparseable)
if err != null {
  .error = "could not parse the unparseable"
  .error_msg = err
}
```

title: `validate_json_schema` - Missing JSON schema file causes panic
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

The implementation of `validate_json_schema` requires that the referenced JSON schema file be accessible _at function call compile time_, rather than merely at runtime / evaluation time. If the given JSON schema file path is inaccessible, VRL and Vector will panic, causing a total app crash.

I believe the intention would be to merely throw a VRL function error at runtime.

### VRL Program

```text
valid, err = validate_json_schema(s'{"hi":1}', "some/bad/path/json-schema.json")
```

title: When parsing CEF, the escaped | in the CEF header is not parsed correctly
body:
If a pipe (|) is used in the header, it must be escaped with a backslash (\). But note that the pipes in the extension do not need escaping. For example:

`{
	"message": "CEF:1|Product|Vendor|7|operation1\\|operation2|Information|Unknown|eventId=7685828129 msg=MessageTest"
}`

Result `. = parse_cef!(.message)` on https://playground.vrl.dev:

`{
	"cefVersion": "1",
	"deviceEventClassId": "operation1|operation2",
	"deviceProduct": "Vendor",
	"deviceVendor": "Product",
	"deviceVersion": "7",
	"eventId": "7685828129",
	"msg": "Message",
	"name": "Information",
	"severity": "Unknown"
}`

The same message processed by vector 0.48.0 (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc a67e4e2 2025-06-30 18:25:45.272082383) gives the following result:

	"deviceVersion": "7",

title: Feature Request: Recursive Function Support in Remap for OTLP Attribute Transformation

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
The structure of attributes within OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) can be complex, as seen in examples like this: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-proto/blob/main/examples/logs.json#L23.

We are currently using Vector to transform OTLP data into a flattened JSON format for ingestion into ClickHouse. To achieve this flattened JSON, recursive function calls are necessary to navigate and process the nested OTLP attribute structure.

However, Vector's remap transform currently lacks the ability to declare functions, which prevents us from implementing the required recursion directly within remap configuration. As a workaround, we are forced to use Lua for this specific transformation.

Would it be possible to add support for function declaration (and thus recursive function calls) within the remap transform? This feature would significantly simplify our configuration and reduce the need for external scripting languages like Lua for common data transformation tasks involving complex nested structures.

title: New function: haversine (map distances on globe between latitude/longitude pairs)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

We enrich data with MMDB data sets, giving us lat/lon for event data. We plot events on a globe/map with rough location of client and rough location of endpoint (could be POP, could be a target host, could be a target nameserver looked up in an enrichment CSV.)  Events will have higher or lower "value" based on distance, or will be treated differently in visibility tooling based on distance.  In order to calculate this, we need a Haversine function to compute distance between two lat/lon pairs and insert that into each event at the edge of the telemetry system instead of doing post-processing.

### Attempted Solutions

External computation is possible, but requires looping events through some generic code, so that is basically a non-starter for us.

### Proposal

I propose a function called "haversine" that takes two lat/lon points, and a measurement system (miles, kilometers) and emits a distance and a bearing on the earth.

```
haversine(measurement:<miles|kilometers>, lat1:<latitude1>, lon1:<longitude1>, lat2:<latitude2>, lon2:<longitude2>)
```
This results in an object containing:
distance (numeric distance between lat1/lon1 and lat2/lon2 within 7 decimals of exactness.)
bearing (degrees of bearing between point1 and point2 with three decimal degrees of exactness)


latitudes and longitudes are real numbers which will be used to within 7 decimal places of exactness.

This might require a new function class called "Map Functions" in the documentation (https://vector.dev/docs/reference/vrl/functions/)

title: `find` should return `null` when the pattern wasn't found
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

Discussed in https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/discussions/1311

Right now it returns `-1`, which from what I can see is somewhat of a special case, because in other functions if something could not be found, `null` is returned. Returning `-1` might introduce hidden bugs if the return value is not analyzed, for example:

```
input = "foobar"
index = find!(input, "123")
output = slice!(input, index)
assert_eq!(output, "r")
```
This code will compile without issues, and the value stored in `output` will be `"r"`. Maybe it would be better to return `null` (which will fail the `slice!()` function) or make the `find!()` function fail if the pattern wasn't found, requiring the developer to handle that case explicitly.

### VRL Program

```text
input = "foobar"
index = find!(input, "123")

title: Should is_nullish([]) and is_nullish({}) return true?

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->

Currently, `is_nullish([])` and `is_nullish({})` will return `false`.

Now, there is of course `is_empty()`, but there's also `is_null()`. There are many cases where one is not only just concerned with "populated" strings, but also "populated" arrays and maps/objects without knowing what explicit type it is.

Per the documentation for `is_nullish()`:

> Determines whether value is nullish, where nullish denotes the *absence of a meaningful value*.

_(emphasis added)_

IMHO `is_nullish([])` and `is_nullish({})` should return `true` to be consistent with/parallel to the pattern/behavior/relation/intent of `is_empty("")` ↔ `is_nullish("")`, and more in line with the stated design intent of `is_nullish()`.

This is/would be, of course, unfortunately a breaking change but it is arguably a more "correct" implementation.

### Use Cases

Given the following data:

<details>
<summary>`data.json`</summary>

```json
{"log":{"items":[{"foo":null},{"foo":""},{"foo":[]},{"foo":{}},{"foo":"something happened"},{"foo":["a thing happened","then another thing happened"]},{"foo":{"thing1":"happened!","thing2":"did not happen, shucks"}}]}}
```

Exploded/"pretty", for convenience on human eyes/to save you the `jq` trip:
```json
{
  "log": {
    "items": [
      {
        "foo": null
      },
      {
        "foo": ""
      },
      {
        "foo": []
      },
      {
        "foo": {}
      },
      {
        "foo": "something happened"
      },
      {
        "foo": [
          "a thing happened",
          "then another thing happened"
        ]
      },
      {
        "foo": {
          "thing1": "happened!",
          "thing2": "did not happen, shucks"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

_(As an aside, any chance of getting `vector vrl` working with the exploded/"pretty" form of JSON input? Want a separate issue for that or does one already exist?)_
```

</details>

The following VRL program will *not* do what one would think it does based on the description of `is_nullish()` (liberal use of `log()` instead of `assert()` to make sure all cases are demonstrated without abort):

<details>
<summary>`test.vrl`</summary>

```
log("BEGIN")

items = array!(.log.items)

for_each(items) -> |idx, item| {

  val = item.foo

  path_str = ".log.items.[" + to_string(idx) + "].foo"

  log_ins_str = " "
  target = false
  if idx < 4 {
    log_ins_str = " no "
    target = true
  }

  evald = is_nullish(val)

  n = evald == target

  log(
	"\n
	Path " + path_str + " has" + log_ins_str + "meaningful data.
	Value: " + encode_json(val, false) + "
	Target: " + to_string(target) + "
	Evaluated: " + to_string(evald) + "
	Confirmed: " + to_string(n) + "
	\n",
  rate_limit_secs: 0
  )
}

log("END")
```

</details>

### Attempted Solutions

The only alternative currently for an *accurate* and *correct* evaluation of whether an array or map/object has meaningful data is to first check:

```
if (is_array(item) || is_object(item)) && is_empty(item) { ... }`
```

which is kind of a PITA, especially if the value can ALSO be a string, which **then** becomes:

```
if (is_array(item) || is_object(item) || is_string(item)) && is_empty(item) { ... }
```

or

```
if ((is_array(item) || is_object(item) && is_empty(item)) || (is_string(item) && is_nullish(item)) { ... }
```

instead of just:

```
if is_nullish(item) { ... }
```

for all three types.

### Proposal

As stated above, `is_nullish([])` and `is_nullish({})` should return `true` instead of `false`.

### References

_No response_

title: VRL: add `main` log format for `parse_nginx_log`
body:
### Use Cases

The `parse_nginx_log` function currently supports the following formats:

- `combined`
- `error`
- `ingress_nginx`

The official Docker images for Nginx come with a default configuration file using the `main` format, defined as:

```nginx
    log_format  main  '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" '
                      '$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" '
                      '"$http_user_agent" "$http_x_forwarded_for"';
```

### Reference

These configuration files are provided by the [Nginx Linux Packages](https://nginx.org/en/linux_packages.html) repositories, and the corresponding source packages are located in the [pkg-oss](https://hg.nginx.org/pkg-oss) repository:

- [alpine/alpine/nginx.conf](https://hg.nginx.org/pkg-oss/file/tip/alpine/alpine/nginx.conf)
- [debian/debian/nginx.conf](https://hg.nginx.org/pkg-oss/file/tip/debian/debian/nginx.conf)
- [rpm/SOURCES/nginx.conf](https://hg.nginx.org/pkg-oss/file/tip/rpm/SOURCES/nginx.conf)

### Related work
- #5 and #193

title: Allow `parse_duration` function to parse multiple duration similar to Golang's `time.ParseDuration`

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Hi, I would like to add the feature for VRL, which is allow `parse_duration` function to parse give string with multiple units such as `1h1s`, and `3s3ms` and so on similar to golang's [time.ParseDuration](https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.23.4:src/time/format.go;l=1617).

Basically, golang's implementation parse given string until finding the duration unit, and keeps finding next digit unit match next duration unit. So, space is not allowed in the given duration string in golang. But since space is already allowed in VRL's `parse_duraiton`. I think space could be added for multiple-units duration string.
However, golang's implementation allows sign for given duration string. Whether we should add the support for signed duration deserves another issue opened.

title: Move core VRL documentation out of Vector

labels.name: type:tech debt
labels.description: A code change that does not add user value

labels.name: domain:dev
labels.description: Anything related to the development environment

labels.name: domain:ci
labels.description: Anything related to Vector's CI environment

body:
All of the documentation describing VRL actually lives in the Vector repository as part of the [remap reference manual](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/tree/master/website/cue/reference/remap). This results in the complication where a change to VRL requires changing both repositories in order to keep the documentation aligned.

It would be helpful for development experience to move the documentation for VRL into this repository such that changes to the core of VRL do not require corresponding changes to Vector other than pulling in the new revision dependency. This will, of course, require building up at least a little infrastructure here to check and possibly format the docs during building and/or CI.

title: Add functions to map an array into an object

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
When manipulating data that has been parsed from CSV or other columnar data sources, it is useful to be able to map those columns into an object with named fields. I propose adding two functions to accomplish this, mirroring the approach in Python: `object` and `zip`:

* `zip` takes a number of arrays as input and produces a single array as output containing a tuple of elements from each array. For example `zip([1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9])` returns `[[1,4,7],[2,5,8],[3,6,9]]`.
* `object` takes takes a zipped array as above with (key, value) pairs and produces an object as output. For example `object([["foo":1],["bar":2]])` returns `{"foo":1,"bar":2}`.

title: feat(stdlib): Function for Converting Character Encodings

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Our system utilizes both legacy systems and the latest Linux distributions. Occasionally, we encounter systems that operate with non-UTF-8 settings. When logs are sent via TCP from these systems, all Korean strings encoded in EUC-KR become corrupted.

To address this issue, I've created a functions.
The function signature is as follows.
```vrl
decode_charset(value, from_charset)
encode_charset(value, to_charset)
```

If this addition is beneficial for the VRL project, I would like to submit a pull request.

title: to_float and infinity result can crash vector
body:
We ran into an issue where parsing a string with `to_float` exceeds the bounds of `f64::MAX`, which returns a non-error infinity value.
```
$ str_value = ""
""

$ parsed_value, err = to_float(str_value)
inf

$ err
null
```
Since `err` was `null`, it's might seem like it's safe to perform operations on this value but subtraction causes vector to panic and crash. This is because `f64::INFINITY - f64::INFINITY == f64::NAN` in rust.
```
$ parsed_value + parsed_value
inf

$ parsed_value + 1
inf

$ parsed_value - 1
inf

$ 1 - parsed_value
-inf

$ parsed_value - parsed_value
thread 'main' panicked at /Users/dan.hable/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/ordered-float-4.2.2/src/lib.rs:1331:37:
Subtraction resulted in NaN: FloatIsNan
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```
I can't find anything in the VRL language, besides using `to_string` to compare with "inf", that would allow me to detect this situation and avoid operations on infinite values. IMHO, I would have expected an error result instead of infinity, similar to how `to_int` behaves.
```
$ parsed_value, err = to_int(str_value)
"function call error for \"to_int\" at (20:29): Invalid integer \"\": number too large to fit in target type"
```

title: object() is only sometimes fallible
body:
Related to another issue, I'm running into a funny problem where the `object()` function is only sometimes fallible.

In an earlier transform, `.` has been turned into an object. Now in a new transform, we run into the following problems:

Fails `vector validate` because `.` is considered of type `any`:
```
redact(., filters: [...])
```

Ok, no problem. We'll ensure it's an object first! The following passes `vector validate` but now fails when tests are executed because `object!()` is considered infallible:

```
original = object!(.)
redact(original, filters: [...])
```

That's strange, because the docs mark `object()` as a fallible function. Ok, well, we could try to handle the error, but this doesn't work either because errors aren't returned for infallible functions:

```
original, err = object(.)
if err != null {
  abort
}
```

The reason seems to be that `object()` is considered _sometimes_ fallible:

```rust
impl FunctionExpression for ObjectFn {
    fn resolve(&self, ctx: &mut Context) -> Resolved {
        object(self.value.resolve(ctx)?)
    }

    fn type_def(&self, state: &state::TypeState) -> TypeDef {
        self.value
            .type_def(state)
            .fallible_unless(Kind::object(Collection::any()))
            .restrict_object()
    }
}
```

Given that I'm not sure how to actually use the function. It is only possible to get a passing `vector validate` and `vector test` if you pass a non-object, e.g. `object("definite-not-an-object")` so that it can be fallible for test+validate. If an object is passed in, it's still fallible for validate, but becomes infallible for test.

title: Add `parse_influxdb` function
body:
With the merge of https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/pull/19637, we thought of using that decoder instead of a custom lua one (which takes a lot of cpu), but it seems that we have malformed line protocol messages and using the `decoding.codec=influxdb` option in sources does allow to route the malformed messages somewhere else, as the data is being dropped.

The alternative we see is to use a remap transform with a `parse_influxdb` function and `drop_on_abort=true`, so we can route the malformed data (`<component_id>.dropped`) to our custom lua decoder which is less strict.

In order to handle this failing line protocol messages, we think that a `parse_influxdb` vrl function is needed. The implementation should be very similar to https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/210ff0925d391213556f07bf6ce621967f0368ca/lib/codecs/src/decoding/format/influxdb.rs#L97 

Doubt: The source decoder option is `decoding.codec=influxdb` and not `decoding.codec=line_protocol`, shoud we call this function `parse_influxdb` in order to be consistent with the vector option? or should we change the vector config spec to use `decoding.codec=line_protocol`?

### Problem


Vector panics at timestamp conversation to_unix_timestamp and crashes. Log messages:

```
vector[582913]: thread 'vector-worker' panicked at 'value can not be represented in a timestamp with nanosecond precision.', /cargo/registry/src/index.crates>

INFO vector: Vector has stopped.
```

We found out that it was a very small date in some of the logs. This one message has crashed all our 3 aggregators. How: we have Kafka between agents and aggregators, one message crashed first vector and was not consumed, then other two after rebalancing tried to consume this message and also crashed. All 3 aggregators were continuously restarting every 10 seconds, until our fix in VRL.

      if err != null {

```

Some software encodes 128-bit UUIDs using base62, but a lot of software expects to see the traditional hyphenated base16 encoding of these identifiers. A user currently needs to fallback to lua for this since VRL is unable to perform the transformation. It would be helpful  to have a function `uuidFromBase62` that takes a string argument and returns a string (with the possibility of failure). Here is a concrete example of the expected behavior:

```
Argument: "3s87yEvnmkiPBMHsj8bwwc"
Result: "7f41deed-d5e2-8b5e-7a13-ab4ff93cfad2"
```

Failure should occur in any of these cases:

* the byte sequence represented by the argument is more than 16 bytes long
* the arguments contains characters not in the class `[0-9A-Za-Z]`

I'm probably going to need to roll this on my own soon so that I can get data into clickhouse (which expects UUIDs as hyphenated base16 json strings). I would appreciate any feedback on the name or overall design, or any feedback that would make it more likely that would increase the likelihood that I can upstream this work. Thanks.

Hello, 


I am parsing syslog messages, parsing them to OTEL format, and then posting to OTEL http endpoint, and this works.
But, the caveat is that I had to set buffer size to 1, which is less than ideal.

This is my config file

```toml
 [sources.my_syslog_source]
   type = "file"
   include = ["/var/log/syslog"] # Replace with the path to your syslog file
   ignore_older = 120 # Optional: Ignore files older than 2 minutes

 [transforms.my_log_transformer]
   type = "remap"
   inputs = ["my_syslog_source"]
   ## format for OTEL logs
   source = '''
stuctured =   parse_syslog!(.message)
messageJson = parse_json!(stuctured.message)

.resourceLogs = [
    {
        "resource": {
            "attributes": [{
                "key":"service.name",
                "value" : {
                    "stringValue": stuctured.appname
                }
            }]
        },
        "scopeLogs":[{
             "scope": {},
              "logRecords": [{
                 "timeUnixNano": messageJson.timestamp,
                 "severityText": messageJson.level,
                 "body": {
                    "stringValue": messageJson.message
                 },
                 "attributes": [],

                 "spanId": messageJson.span_id
              }]
        }]
        
    }
] 

del(.message)
del(.file)
del(.host)
del(.source_type)
del(.timestamp)
'''

 [sinks.my_otel_sink]
   type = "http"
   inputs = ["my_log_transformer"]
   uri = "https://collector.app/v1/logs" # Replace with your OTel endpoint
   auth.strategy="basic"
   auth.user = "ds"
   auth.password = "user"
   encoding.codec = "json"
   framing.method = "newline_delimited"

[sinks.my_otel_sink.batch]
    max_events = 1
[sinks.my_otel_sink.buffer]
    type="disk"
    max_size= 1073741824 # 1GiB.
    when_full="drop_newest"

[sinks.my_otel_sink.request]

So this works, but he problem is, that wen buffer has more than one message, it does http POST like this:

title: Add "dns_lookup" function
body:
We have a need to perform lookups on DNS results delivered to us via the DNSTAP source, to determine (as an example) if an error is transient, or is related to a specific geography of resolvers that may be malfunctioning. Also, some DNS requests may yield lookup data in some cases, where a TXT or other result can be used to enrich the logging message as it moves through Vector, or where NS records may be used to enrich data such as "What authoritative nameserver cluster provided these answers?"

We would therefore like to request this as a VRL feature to be added to Vector that allows DNS requests to be emitted from Vector, and the result of those queries to be handed back in some easily parseable way.   The good news is that there already exists a DNSTAP structure, and so this would require grafting an existing Rust-based resolver library to produce results that could be fed to the DNSTAP parser as replies.

There are caveats here, and that is understood. These may be slow processes - the DNS is not easily predicted for response times. Local caches should be used, possibly on the same server as Vector is operating, in order to accelerate results. Timeouts and retries for failures should probably be kept low as a best-practice - "fail fast."  Simply because this may be slow is not sufficient to not perform the lookups - we will probably execute these on a sampled set of events in order to tune an adequate response rate to the stream of total inbound events we need to parse.

This would specifically not allow queries for QTYPEs of AXFR, IXFR, or ANY as they are too complex to easily render and are difficult to imagine in a Vector use case.

Ideally these fields would be used:

 - qname (mandatory)
 - QTYPE (mandatory)
 - namesever destination (optional - if not specified, system resolver will be used)
 - options (optional)
 - class (optional, default IN)

The reply from the resolver code would be handed back as a DNSTAP message structure.

Example:

`.myDnsResult = dns_lookup!("www.example.com", "9.9.9.9", "A", ["timeout=1", "tries=1", "nodnssec", "nsid"])
`

Errors in the DNS lookup should not produce errors within Vector, unless they are invalid command options which cannot be parsed. NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIl, etc. are all legitimate responses from the resolver stack, and should be represented in the DNSTAP message and not raise an error in Vector.  Only if the syntax of the command is incorrect should the lookup fail with an error outcome that is fallible, or if there is a timeout in the response (should this be a fixed number like 5 seconds?) or if there is some problem executing the command like no sockets available or no route to IP address for the recursive resolver.

This option list cribbed from recent Debian "dig" options that seem relevant and which are not redundant:

Options:
```
   [no]aaflag         (Set AA flag in query ([no]aaflag))
   [no]adflag         (Set AD flag in query (default on))
   [no]badcookie      (Retry BADCOOKIE responses)
   bufsize[=###]      (Set EDNS0 Max UDP packet size)
   [no]cdflag         (Set checking disabled flag in query)
   [no]cookie         (Add a COOKIE option to the request)
   [no]dns64prefix    (Get the DNS64 prefixes from ipv4only.arpa)
   [no]dnssec         (Request DNSSEC records)
   [no]edns[=###]     (Set EDNS version) [0]
   ednsflags=###      (Set EDNS flag bits)
   [no]ednsnegotiation (Set EDNS version negotiation)
   ednsopt=###[:value] (Send specified EDNS option)
   noednsopt          (Clear list of ednsopt options)
   [no]expire         (Request time to expire)
   [no]fail           (Don't try next server on SERVFAIL)
   [no]header-only    (Send query without a question section)
   [no]ignore         (Don't revert to TCP for TC responses.)
   ndots=###          (Set search NDOTS value)
   [no]nsid           (Request Name Server ID)
   [no]nssearch       (Search all authoritative nameservers)
   [no]opcode=###     (Set the opcode of the request)
   padding=###        (Set padding block size [0])
   qid=###            (Specify the query ID to use when sending queries)
   [no]raflag         (Set RA flag in query ([no]raflag))
   [no]recurse        (Recursive mode ([no]rdflag))
   retry=###          (Set number of UDP retries) [2]
   subnet=addr        (Set edns-client-subnet option)
   [no]tcflag         (Set TC flag in query)
   [no]tcp            (TCP mode)
   timeout=###        (Set query timeout) [5]
   tries=###          (Set number of UDP attempts) [3]
   [no]zflag          (Set Z flag in query)

title: Add "sieve" string function
body:
It would be useful to have a method to remove characters from strings which are undesired or un-necessary for parsing of data (typically distilling to human-readable data fields.)  This would eliminate or replace characters that have special (dangerous) meaning to downstream consumers, or which are not presentable in other formats. 

Purposes for this function are multiple: it provides an additional layer of safety for downstream systems which may not handle characters appropriately; it may reduce the volume of data where there are large numbers of unprintable or unstructured characters in a message; it may make more readable certain messages that contain excessive numbers of extraneous characters.

I would propose the function name of "sieve" for this function, and at first glance I would imagine three arguments:

  - string to act upon (required)
  - set of characters to permit, in example form:   [A-z],[0-9], \,, ü, 0xE282AC  (required) 
     - this would be ranges of ASCII or UTF-8 
     - actual characters embedded in config file (is this legal in Vector configs?)
     - hexadecimal UTF-8 
     - escaped (\) special characters
  - character to insert/overwrite single instances of deleted results in output (default is to delete all characters other than sieve list.) Can be explicitly set to "" to delete characters with no replacement. (optional)
  - character to insert/overwrite when two or more sequential instances of deleted characters are in input string. Can be explicitly set to "" to delete characters with no replacement. (optional)

title: Feature request: CDB for enrichment table source
body:
We currently use DJB's Constant DataBase (CDB - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cdb_(software) )   as a source for matching lists in our DNS environment, in the "front-end" systems that see hundreds of thousands or millions of requests per second.  It's quite performant, especially coupled with caching by the local application that is performing the queries.

In the logging stream (DNSTAP) we would also like to use CDB, as this would require no conversion of some of our existing tooling, and would be well-suited for large data set matching and enrichment that would be specific to how we envision using Vector. 

Note: it is fairly trivial to turn CDB into CSV, which might match well with the existing Vector CSV enrichment system. That can mean one of two (or more) options: make the user turn CDB into CSV to avoid the development work, or create an adapter that treats CDB files as CSV and simply converts them at load time. (https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/13b914781b3c118cbf867609ebab5d5fc6a525dc/rfcs/2021-07-20-8288-csv-enrichment.md) 

I do have a question about CSV functionality, which is why I reference CDB: how are reloads managed? CDB files handle switchout for new data sets exceptionally well, and that is implicit in CDB's model. CSV files as enrichment sources in Vector are less clear - CSV is loaded into memory, but how is that updated without a full restart?

Meta-summary:

Basic desired functionality;
 - Lookup key in CDB, return multi-value results
 - Cache answers (including "no match") for N milliseconds or until CDB file changes (datestamp/size) as checked every N seconds, for performance

There seem to be Rust implementations of CDB, but again I'll not put any suggestions in here as my search-engine based answers in no way should resemble development ideas.  :-)

title: Feature request: detect, parse punycode for DNS IDN objects
body:
Any system that digests DNS data for more than a few hostnames will eventually get IDN names (https://unicode.org/faq/idn.html) in the data stream. This quickly presents problems for back-end data store and monitoring systems.

Systems may choose to keep IDN in their existing form, but having the ability to add fields which are encoded in punycode (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punycode) is desirable, as many DNS logging systems expect and use punycode to simplify management of handling IDN objects.

There are two three things which I think would be useful to have in Vector:
 - the ability to detect if a field contains characters which are present in IDN-formatted strings
 - the ability to convert IDN names into punycode from UTF-8
 - the ability to convert IDN names from punycode into UTF-8

There appear to be several existing Rust libraries which do this type of conversion. I don't know which have what desirable features or preferred licenses, so I won't make references here so as not to bias any search.

Notes: 
  - this is DNS-specific.  The conversion would have to be applied to each "zone cut" between periods, but portions of the name that do not have UTF-8 would not be translated.  So www.café.com would be www.xn--caf-dma.com as an example.
  -  lowercasing the name is automatically assumed.  So www.CAFé.com and www.cafÉ.com would also be www.xn--caf-dma.com

title: Feature request: public suffix (TLD and ETLD+1) parsing

labels.name: good first issue
labels.description: Anything that is good for new contributors

body:
We're using DNSTAP for ingestion of DNS data. One of the data fields that we're interested in storing separately in our archive is the TLD and ETLD+1 data, which means the top level domain (".com", ".ch", ".xyz") which is trivially easy, but also the portion of the domain which is the part that is handled by a registrar.  For .com, as an example, it is the name immediately to the left of ".com" - so "example.com" is ETLD+1 for the .com zone.  For other regions of the DNS, this break point is non-obvious, and the Mozilla Public Suffix Iist (PSL) is the well-known authority on defining where those domain breaks occur so that the correct number of zone cuts can be made to capture the ETLD+1.  I imagine that many logfiles have domain-based data in them that would be interesting to parse in this manner - not just DNSTAP-oriented data.

Doing this computation at the edge of our telemetry pipeline makes the most sense for us.  Vector seems like a good place to do it, but there is currently no function that does this. 

There is a Rust library for this functionality (https://github.com/1Password/passkey-rs/tree/main/public-suffix) but what the command/function would look like from within VRL is not immediately obvious to me so I won't make suggestions as to how it could look in any detail. The short form: It would be useful to have a function that would result with the TLD and ETLD+1 for a given Fully-Qualified Domain Name provided as input.  Or even a ETLD+N where "N" is define-able.

title: Feature request: decode_protobuf  (parse_protobuf?)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
We have found ourselves in a situation where there is protobuf messaging being encoded into a field inside another protobuf message.  There are a variety of helpful features in Vector now that perform "decode" functions on data-within-data, but not something that I can currently see which would decode protobuf messages embedded into objects.  Perhaps this might be useful to others as well.

I would expect a definition (file path?) of the .proto file would have to be provided as part of the function call.

(would a better term here be "parse_protobuf" instead of "decode_protobuf"?  I'm not sure where each term would be applied in this situation.)

To be entirely feature complete, it would be ideal for a patch be able to put protobuf messages back into protobuf fields, but that is not something we need to do and we would be ENTIRELY satisfied to have it just be a decode process and not an encode process as well.  :-)

title: parse_nginx_log fails on empty referer
body:
Hello,

it seems pattern definition for nginx common log used by parse_nginx_log function expects non-empty referer: https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/blob/2b39353b3236e0aac26314ad47153238c52aa2ff/src/stdlib/log_util.rs#L136C1-L136C106

As it turns out, in practice, referer can be empty, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/6880659/in-what-cases-will-http-referer-be-empty. E.g. when the enduser
> entered the site URL in browser address bar itself.
    visited the site by a browser-maintained bookmark.
    visited the site as first page in a new window/tab/session, in some browsers.
    clicked a link on a page having restrictive [<meta name="referrer">](http://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/Meta_referrer) tag.
    clicked a link on a page having restrictive [Referrer-Policy](https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/) header.
    clicked a link having [rel="noreferrer"](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/noreferrer).
    clicked a link in an external application (i.e. not a webbrowser, e.g. Flash).
    switched from a https URL to a http URL.
    has security software installed (antivirus/firewall/etc) which strips the referrer from all requests.
    is behind a proxy which strips the referrer from all requests.
    visited the site programmatically (like, curl) without setting the referrer header (bots!).

This means that any time we get client request with empty referer, vector fails to parse nginx log line. We do get thousands of these issues each day.

Example code for vrl playground (vrl 0.9.1, vector cebe6284).

Working:
https://playground.vrl.dev/?%3D

Broken: 
https://playground.vrl.dev/?%3D%3D

title: regex replace using a closure
body:
I filed https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/issues/633, but now realize that this might have been a better place to report it. 

For convenience I will copy over my text from there:

### Use Cases

I want to redact certain personally identifiable information, such as an email address, from logs, but in such a way that if I already know the information (email address), I can search the logs for matching log entries. 

### Attempted Solutions

I think it would be possible to do this with a lua transform. But  the documentation for that says to create an issue if the remap transform doesn't meet my needs.

Lua also doesn't have a built in sha256 function so I would either need to use a lua native sha256 implementation, which I suspect would be slow, or pull in a shared library that adds such a function for lua (is that possible with vector?)

### Proposal

I can think of a few ways this could be done:

- Add an option to the redact function that will replace the matched string with a hash of itself, Possibly with a configurable hash function, instead of with a fixed string.
- add a new function  that replaces a matching regex with its hash
- make a function like replace, but instead of a string for the replacement, it uses a closure to compute a replacement value.

I think that the last bullet point is the most general and could be useful in other cases as well. 

P.s. having a built in redaction pattern for email addresses would be awesome.

title: How to merge two `TypeState`/`LocalEnv` including the `bindings`?
body:
My use case for VRL is to allow multiple `Program`s to run serially, and I have a shared `RuntimeState` that allows me to share the runtime state. 
I also want to allow variables to be shared across `Program`s. To do that, I'm using `compile_with_state` and passing the previous state. But in the case of >2 `Program`s, I need to merge the `TypeState` of multiple `Program`s. 

```
# Program 1: this one works obviously
my_var1 = "1"

# Program 2: this one also works, because I only need to use a single TypeState (from program 1)
my_var2 = "2"
log("my_var1: " + my_var1 + "my_var2: " + my_var2);

# Program 3: This one fails because "merge" doesn't work as expected
log("my_var1: " + my_var1 + "my_var2: " + my_var2);
```

I tried to use the `LocalEnv::merge` function, but it seems like it's merging the `details` only, without merging the `bindings` vector together:
https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/blob/59fb310809ac7bb9f2e1b137d10ca4178a4e5625/src/compiler/state.rs#L87-L93

I suspect that `LocalEnv::merge` might have a bug because it does not merge the complete `bindings` vectors. I tried to work around it but it seems like all functions and properties are `pub(crate)` so I can't seem to create the `LocalEnv` manually with the data I need. 
I created a PR to address this issue: https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/pull/596

Introducing a `pretty` parameter to the `encode_json` function would be beneficial as it enables pretty print support for JSON output. 
When the `pretty` parameter is set to `true`, the function will utilize `serde_json::to_string_pretty` to generate indented and human-readable JSON.

title: Auto-generate VRL function documentation

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem
Before the VRL repo was split from Vector, VRL function documentation was manually added for each change in CUE docs. Now since the repo is split, there is currently no way to add / update documentation with each PR. Even before, it was easy for documentation to become out of date since it's manually updated and nothing is checking it for accuracy.

## Proposal
The source of documentation will live wherever VRL functions are defined. (The VRL repo for stdlib functions, or other repos for user added functions, such as Vector specific VRL functions). This will be auto-generated directly from the code (function name, parameters, examples, .etc) and supplemented by annotations were needed. This will be roughly similar to Vector's [config schema](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/master/rfcs/2022-02-23-9481-config-schema.md)

The VRL repo will contain a tool that can generate a computer-readable intermediate format of the function documentation in JSON. This allows end-users of VRL to generate documentation from the intermediate format.

For example:
- Vector would generate the intermediate JSON format for the stdlib functions, as well as several Vector specific functions, and then convert that to CUE docs for the documentation [here](https://vector.dev/docs/reference/vrl/functions/)
- VRL itself may one day host it's own documentation for just the stdlib. The intermediate format gives flexibility to use whatever tool makes sense for the job, instead of having to copy what Vector is currently using.
- The VRL playground (or Observability Pipelines) could ingest this data as they wish to improve the related UI.
- Future users of VRL could integrate this data into their own documentation.

All of the sidelined logs have `unknown` as the value for the `account-id` column, which is [listed as possible in the AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html#flow-logs-default).

VRL [appears to type account-id as an int64](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/blob/2bbe6728fc0a9d0c20b6ee8634346bdbf28f78d8/src/stdlib/parse_aws_vpc_flow_log.rs#L194), which makes it fail to parse any VPC Flow logs where the account id is unknown. I believe parsing as int64 will also drop any leading `0` characters, which would make the output incorrect for any account id that has one or more leading zeroes.

Sample log with ENI and IPs obfuscated:
```
2 unknown eni-070b1422222222222 192.168.1.1 10.0.0.2 55828 60002 6 1 44 1685727399 1685727446 ACCEPT OK
```

Let me know if you need any additional information!

title: `encode_zlib` `compression_level` isn't validated which can lead to a panic
body:
Using a compression level higher than 10 will trigger a panic in the `encode_zlib` function. This should be checked by VRL and return an error instead. This will require the function to be fallible (unless the `compression_level` is a valid constant value)

Example
```coffee
encode_zlib("d",66)
```
```sh
thread 'main' panicked at 'assertion failed: level.level() <= 10', /home/nathan/.cargo/registry/src/github.com-1ecc6299db9ec823/flate2-1.0.26/src/ffi/rust.rs:129:9
```

VRL version `main` (`1ff642dc940c7d07`)

I've tried parse_groks, with some success..but for some reason parsing the run_id does not seem to work for me:

source = '''

```

title: Deprecate `to_timestamp` function
body:
Deprecate and remove `to_timestamp` function.

Reasoning from https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/issues/7#issuecomment-1503761940

> After some discussion on the team, we think having the to_timestamp function have a list of "known formats" does more harm than good since there isn't a clear rule we can apply for what formats qualify to be included. Instead, we'd like to push users to use the parse_timestamp function where they supply the format. Additionally, the to_timestamp function has a parameter, units, for interpreting integer values that we also think is a bit odd and would be better served via a specialized from_unix_timestamp function.

Depends on https://github.com/vectordotdev/vrl/issues/188 being done first.

title: Add `from_unix_timestamp` function
body:
Add a `from_unix_timestamp` function that takes the place of the `to_timestamp` function's handling of integer timestamps to be more clear for users.

title: VRL: Add ingress-nginx log format for `parse_nginx_log`

labels.name: good first issue
labels.description: Anything that is good for new contributors

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

Hey guys,

Currently there are only two log formats supported by `parse_nginx_log` function: "combined" and "error".
There's one more ingress-nginx controller default log format described [here](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/user-guide/nginx-configuration/log-format/).

```
log_format upstreaminfo
    '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" '
    '$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" "$http_user_agent" '
    '$request_length $request_time [$proxy_upstream_name] [$proxy_alternative_upstream_name] $upstream_addr '
    '$upstream_response_length $upstream_response_time $upstream_status $req_id';
```

While the beginning of the format is pretty much the same as "combined" described [here](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_log_module.html#log_format):

```
log_format combined '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] '
                    '"$request" $status $body_bytes_sent '
                    '"$http_referer" "$http_user_agent"';
```
I believe there is an intention to make different default formats to parse them separately, like for example

```
structured, err = parse_nginx_log(.message, "ingress_upstreaminfo")
```

as discussed briefly in this [issue](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/issues/6103#issuecomment-762893997)

Anyways, in general it would be much easier for all kubernetes users who uses ingress-nginx in clusters to use `parse_nginx_log` instead of making their own regular expressions for a pretty default log format

* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

`parse_regex` and `parse_regex_all` are accepting the parameter to be only regex. Though the regex can be stored in a variable or resolved on the fly by the `to_regex` function. At the moment this is supported only by `match` function.

### Attempted Solutions

Tried in different ways and the only possible option is to pass regex directly as an argument, like: `parse_regex(r'')`

### Proposal

An option to pass the regex parameter as a variable or as a result of another function (so called group). e.g. `parse_regex(to_regex("some_regex"))` or `my_regex = r''; parse_regex(my_regex)`

### References

Here is the issue which introduced the `to_regex` function https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/issues/7051

### Version

0.28.0

title: "to_timestamp" should recognize TIMESTAMP_ISO8601 grok-pattern

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

"to_timestamp" does not recognize TIMESTAMP_ISO8601 pattern/format is.
"parse_grok" honors  [TIMESTAMP_ISO8601 pattern](https://github.com/daschl/grok/tree/master/patterns), but "to_timestamp" does not.

I would suggest to recognize the same pattern in both "to_timestamp" and "parse_grok"-patterns, so that a .timestamp can be matched and extracted from any field without the need to use parse_timestamp custom formats when the parse_grok did already match on an existing pattern.



### Attempted Solutions


In VRL tested:
```
$ . = { "@timestamp": "2023-01-10T05:05:05.55Z", "@metadata": { "beat": "filebeat", "type": "_doc", "version": "7.9.2" }, "host": { "name": "somehostname" }, "message": "2023-01-10 10:03:30.745 blah blah blah blah" }
{ "@metadata": { "beat": "filebeat", "type": "_doc", "version": "7.9.2" }, "@timestamp": "2023-01-10T05:05:05.55Z", "host": { "name": "somehostname" }, "message": "2023-01-10 10:03:30.745 blah blah blah blah" }

$ .flat = parse_grok!(.message, "^%{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:datestamp} %{GREEDYDATA:logline}")
{ "datestamp": "2023-01-10 10:03:30.745", "logline": "blah blah blah blah" }

$ .timestamp = to_timestamp!(.flat.datestamp)
function call error for "to_timestamp" at (13:43): No matching timestamp format found for "2023-01-10 10:03:30.745"

$ .timestamp = to_timestamp!(.@timestamp)
t'2023-01-10T05:05:05.550Z'

_No response_

title: `parse_nginx_log` fails for various logged bot requests
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

My nginx default vhost receives a ton of random bot requests every day, some are non-standard requests (http status 400 bad request) and fail to be parsed by `parse_nginx_log(.message, "combined")` even though they are logged properly.

### Configuration

```toml
[transforms.nginx_access_parsed]
type = "remap"
inputs = [ "nginx_access" ]
source = """
structured, err = parse_nginx_log(.message, "combined")
if err != null {
  log((err + "('" + .message + "')") ?? "null", level: "error")
  abort
}

. = merge(., structured)
"""

[[tests]]
name = "nginx access by bot: mglndd"

[[tests.inputs]]
insert_at = "nginx_access_parsed"
type = "log"

    [tests.inputs.log_fields]
    message = "192.241.206.122 - - [18/Sep/2022:10:03:39 +0200] \"MGLNDD_192.241.213.192_443\" 400 150 \"-\" \"-\""
    file = "/var/log/test.example.net/access.log"

[[tests.outputs]]
extract_from = "nginx_access_parsed"

    [[tests.outputs.conditions]]
    type = "vrl"
    source = """
        assert!(is_timestamp(.timestamp))
        assert_eq!(.client, "192.241.206.122")
        assert_eq!(.request, "MGLNDD_192.241.213.192_443")
        assert_eq!(.status, 400)
        assert_eq!(.size, 150)
    """
```


### Version

0.24.1

title: Vector does not parse RFC5424 structured data with some escape characters
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

We've encountered some strange behaviors on VRL function `parse_syslog`, where it discards whole structured data elements if a structured data parameter in structured data contains escape characters (not for all, like `\"`).

When a structured data parameter contains escape character such as `\/`, it then discards whole structured data.

title: Add note to error diagnostics when fallibility is due to function arguments
body:
Users are frequently confused when a function marked is infallible in the docs is fallible because of the types of its arguments. The error message looks like:

```
  error[E103]: unhandled fallible assignment
    ┌─ :7:30
    │
  7 │         .splunk_sourcetype = downcase(type)
    │         -------------------- ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    │         │                    │
    │         │                    this expression is fallible
    │         │                    update the expression to be infallible
    │         or change this to an infallible assignment:
    │         .splunk_sourcetype, err = downcase(type)
    │
    = see documentation about error handling at https://errors.vrl.dev/#handling
    = learn more about error code 103 at https://errors.vrl.dev/103
    = see language documentation at https://vrl.dev
    = try your code in the VRL REPL, learn more at https://vrl.dev/examples
```

I think helpful if the diagnostics mentioned the fallibility is due to the type of the function arguments and, perhaps, included a link to https://vector.dev/docs/reference/vrl/expressions/#function-call-characteristics.

title: VRL: Expand fallibility to include "always fails", and generate a compile time error when this happens

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

Today the concept of fallibility is a boolean. It can either fail, or not fail. It might be useful to expand this to 3 options:
- can't fail
- might fail
- always fails

And in the case where it always fails, a compile time error (or warning) might be useful. Even if this isn't used to generate compile time errors, it can be useful in the future for performance optimizations.

For example, consider the following code. The "start" parameter is known at compile time to always be invalid, but it still compiles.
```coffeescript
slice!("", 1)
```

### Version

0.23.0

title: `split` has odd behavior with negative `limit` parameter
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

## Expected behavior

vrl returns an error.

## Actual behavior

`split` treats `limit` as `usize::MAX` 

```
$ split("This is a long string", " ",  -10000)
["This", "is", "a", "long", "string"]
```

## Notes

The behavior is due to [this cast](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/master/lib/vrl/stdlib/src/split.rs#L6): 

```rust
let limit = limit.try_integer()? as usize;
```
See playground link here: https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=e33b58675012c83493efef2dbb9aa920

```rust
let number = -1_i64 as usize;
dbg!((number, number == usize::MAX));

// [src/main.rs:3] (number, number == usize::MAX) = (
//    18446744073709551615,
//    true,
//)
```

### Version

vector 0.24.0 (x86_64-apple-darwin debug=full)
