title: Closures are compiled assuming they only run exactly once
body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

Closures can be ran any number of times, including none. But type definitions are calculated assuming they run exactly once, which can result in invalid type definitions.

### Example
```coffeescript
$ . = {}
{  }

$ map_values([]) -> |i| {.a = "foo"}
[]

$ type_def(.)
{ "object": { "a": { "bytes": true } } }

$ .
{  }
```


### Version

0.23.0

title: add "must use" warnings for VRL expressions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

Many expressions / functions in VRL return a result rather than modify the input. For example, the `push` function which appends a single element to the end of an array. It is easy to incorrectly assume this may modify the input, and not check the output which results in the expression doing nothing. We could add `#[must_use]` style warnings to VRL to help prevent these types of issues.


### Example user error
```coffeescript
$ .array = []
[]

$ push(.array, "foo")
["foo"]

$ .array
[]
```


### Version

0.23.0

title: VRL function to normalize size units like MiB, KiB, etc. to bytes

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Use Cases

I frequently come across log messages containing sizes using human-readable units such as MB, KB, GB, or MiB, KiB, GiB. Normalizing these to bytes is a prerequisite for comparison and statistical analysis.

### Attempted Solutions

I can do this using an if statement but it adds a lot of repetitive code to every transformation where I need it.

### Proposal

Add a `normalize_bytes` function to VRL that will take a string specifying a size in human readable capacity units and return an integer number of bytes.  The function should:

- Accept a floating point or integer number for the numeric portion
- Accept and convert all of the common abbreviations for a particular capacity unit:
  - K, KB, KiB - kilobytes
  - M, MB, MiB - megabytes
  - G, GB, GiB - gigabytes
  - T, TB, TiB - terabytes
  - And so on...
- Round any fractional bytes obtained from the conversion up to the nearest integer 
- Assume binary units by default (multiples of 1024 instead of 1000)
- Have an optional parameter (`binary`) that when set to false uses multiples of 1000 instead of 1024
- Accept optional whitespace between the number and the unit
- Treat the units case-insensitively

### References

_No response_

### Version

0.22.2

title: Improve module structure of VRL crates

labels.name: type:tech debt
labels.description: A code change that does not add user value

body:
VRL's module structure has grown organically, and has become more unclear as time passed. Especially when implementing stdlib functions, and having to write non-standard tests (in my case, when wanting to write a test that validates closure behaviour), numerous modules have to pulled in from different places, sometimes through `vrl::prelude`, which makes it unclear what is going on.

I'm not proposing removing `prelude` (it's valuable to stdlib authors that aren't as familiar with Rust), but we should trim it, focus it, and also audit all other modules in VRL crates.

title: Add `unflatten` function

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
<!--
Hi there,

Thank you for opening an issue. Please note that we try to keep the Vector issue tracker reserved for bug reports and feature requests. For general usage questions, please see: https://chat.vector.dev.
-->

<!--- Please keep this note for the community --->

### Community Note

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment

<!--- Thank you for keeping this note for the community --->

### Current Vector Version

<!---
Run `vector --version` to show the version, and paste the result between the ``` marks below. This will record which version was current at the time of your feature request, to help manage the request backlog.

If you're not using the latest version, please check to see if something related to your request has already been implemented in a later version.
-->

```
vector 0.19.1 (x86_64-apple-darwin 3cf70cf 2022-01-25)
```

### Use-cases

We have a `flatten` function that flattens objects by joining together nested keys with `.`. It'd be useful to have a way to reverse this. This could also be useful for sources of data that use `.`s in keys.


See https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/discussions/11062

### Attempted Solutions

This `lua` transform works:

```toml
[transforms.nest]
type = "lua"
inputs = ["stdin"]
version = "2"
source = '''
function build_array(...)
  local arr = {}
  for v in ... do
    arr[#arr + 1] = v
  end
  return arr
end

function process(event, emit)
  for key, value in pairs(event.log) do
    event.log[key] = value

    parts = build_array(string.gmatch(key, "[^\\.]+"))

    -- key has a dot in it, break it apart to create nested table
    if #parts > 1 then
      event.log[key] = nil

      to_update = event.log
      for i = 1, #parts - 1 do
        if to_update[parts[i]] == nil then
          to_update[parts[i]] = {}
        end
        to_update = to_update[parts[i]]
      end
      to_update[parts[#parts]] = value
    end
  end
  emit(event)
end
'''
hooks.process = "process"
```

### Proposal

We add a `unflatten` function to VRL that does the opposite of `flatten`.

### References

Are there any other GitHub issues, whether open or closed, that are related to the problem you've described above or to the suggested solution? If so, please create a list below that mentions each of them. For example:

- vectordotdev/vector#7023

-->

That is, this program should work:

```
my_regex = r'(?<Pfoo>e)'
parse_regex("test", my_regex)
```

    starts_with(image, "k8s.gcr.io/kube-scheduler")) {"k8s-plain"}
else {"unknown"}
```

However, we don't allow `else` to appear on a newline by itself without the closing `}`.

We should consider allowing this.

Default (local and global) time zone configurations were added in https://github.com/timberio/vector/pull/6533, with this notable comment:

> Notably absent from the list of transforms is `remap`, which currently always uses the system local time zone. I propose we defer support for configuring this in remap to a separate issue.

I couldn't find this issue (cc @bruceg, my GitHub search-fu might just be lacking), but this was recently asked on Discord, so I figured I'd file this for tracking.

On solving this:

We should do the following steps:

1. Add the time zone config to Vector's `remap` transform.
2. Add the defined time zone to `vrl::Context`.
3. Allow passing in a custom time zone to `Runtime::resolve`.
4. Update time-zone related expressions/functions to take this new piece of context into account.
5. Add tests to validate all of this works as expected.

title: Benchmark Remap change to keep original event

labels.name: domain:vrl
labels.description: Anything related to the Vector Remap Language

body:
We (read: I) merged the change in https://github.com/timberio/vector/pull/6719 without doing any benchmarking to see the impact on performance.

We should measure the impact here, to make sure we're not causing a big drop in performance.

Two things to note here:

- Mutating the event partially when a program fails seems to be something we don't want to have as a default, so the change in that PR still seems to be something we want.
- If a program cannot fail (we can guarantee this at compile/boot-time), _or_ if `drop_on_error` is set to `true` (defaults to `false`), then we don't clone the original event, so there shouldn't be any drop in performance in those cases.
- In any other case, we now keep a copy of the original event for when we need to revert it if the program fails at runtime.

I assigned @jszwedko as I'm not available next week, but anyone else can pick this up as well, or I can do the benchmarking once I'm available again.

title: Remap will overwrite a map rather than add the field to it

labels.name: domain:vrl
labels.description: Anything related to the Vector Remap Language

body:
From the Repl:

```
$ .foo = 3
3

$ .
{ "foo": 3 }

$ .bar = 4
4

$ .
{ "bar": 4 }
```

I would expect when setting `.bar` that it would add that field to the map. It doesn't, it overwrites the entire map.

It should do:

```
$ .foo = 3
3

$ .
{ "foo": 3 }

$ .bar = 4
4

$ .
{ "bar": 4,  "foo": 3 }
```

I believe in the Remap transform, this won't happen with the root object as that is handled differently from `Value::Map` fields. If you try to set the field to any child maps, this will occur.

title: remap-lang: allow querying into result of functions

labels.name: domain:vrl
labels.description: Anything related to the Vector Remap Language

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Improvement or extension to something that already exists.

body:
We currently support querying the root object using paths (e.g. `.foo.bar`) and also variables (`$foo.bar` since #5094).

We've had at least one report thus far requesting to query the result of functions:

```rust
.url = "https://vector.dev"
.scheme = parse_url(.url).scheme // parse_url returns a `Value::Map`
.scheme // "https"
```

I'm not necessarily advocating we support this (it might be a slippery slope from here to supporting methods, although I don't think that's necessarily the case), but it's worth tracking this, given that more people might be looking for a similar feature.

labels.name: domain:vrl
labels.description: Anything related to the Vector Remap Language

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Improvement or extension to something that already exists.

body:
In #5059 we've improved type checking of arithmetic operations to be more exact than before. However, as @FungusHumungus notes in https://github.com/timberio/vector/pull/5059#discussion_r524445777, there is still more we can do to get more precise type information.

For example, `"foo" * 3` is valid, and will always return `"foofoofoo"`, but the type definition of this expression resolves to `Bytes | Integer | Float`, which isn't wrong, but also isn't as accurate as it can be (e.g. `Bytes`).

Additionally, we need to expand our test coverage of the arithmetic expression logic, as there are still some gaps in its functionality.

For example, while `"foo" * 3` works, `3 * "foo"` does not.

title: `regex_parser` transform doesn't work with nested fields

labels.name: good first issue
labels.description: Anything that is good for new contributors.

labels.name: needs:approval
labels.description: Needs review & approval before work can begin.

labels.name: domain:vrl
labels.description: Anything related to the Vector Remap Language

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Improvement or extension to something that already exists.

body:
Currently the `regex` crate which underlies our `regex_parser` implementation supports only `[_0-9a-zA-Z]+` as possible names for captures groups. Thus nested fields of form `x.y.z` cannot be captured.

For example, the following config unit test

```toml
[transforms.regex_parser_nested]
  inputs = []
  type = "regex_parser"
  regex = "^(?P<nested.timestamp>[\\w\\-:\\+]+) (?P<nested.level>\\w+) (?P<doubly.nested.message>.*)$"
[[tests]]
  name = "regex_parser_nested"
  [tests.input]
    insert_at = "regex_parser_nested"
    type = "raw"
    value = "2020-01-01T12:34:56Z INFO hello"
  [[tests.outputs]]
    extract_from = "regex_parser_nested"
    [[tests.outputs.conditions]]
      type = "check_fields"
      "nested.timestamp.equals" = "2020-01-01T12:34:56Z"
      "nested.level.equals" = "INFO"
      "doubly.nested.message.equals" = "hello"
```

fails with the error

```
Failed to build test 'regex_parser_nested':
  failed to build transform 'regex_parser_nested': Invalid regular expression: regex parse error:
      ^(?P<nested.timestamp>[\w\-:\+]+) (?P<nested.level>\w+) (?P<doubly.nested.message>.*)$
                 ^
  error: invalid capture group character
```

I think we need to allow field names containing dots. A simplest option to do this is to fork the `regex` crate and add support for it there, send a PR to the upstream, and use the fork until the support for dots in capture groups in added to the upstream crate.
